correctness.rationale: Subtracting the two stationarity equations gives (I−Pᵀ)(uε−u₀)=ε(uε)ᵢ(eₖ−eⱼ). The restriction to the zero-sum space is invertible by the simplicity of the irreducible stationary eigenvalue, without an aperiodicity assumption. The factor ε(uε)ᵢ is nonzero for a nonzero admissible transfer; the component equation gives the stated positive denominator. The destination-difference columns span precisely the vectors summing to zero on each common-target component, including isolated vertices, so the rank is n−c. Under connectivity the tree columns are a basis; the normalized measured vectors give the inverse on that basis, and the action on the constant vector is already known. Conversion from time occupation to jump visits follows from Qᵀπ=0 and the known positive rates. In the six-state example the row and column sums are one, both triples communicate through states 3 and 4, and cycles through state 1 of lengths 2 and 3 prove period one. The component partition is exactly {1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, so the rank is four. The proof covers exactly admissible probes and noiseless data, not uniformly feasible fixed amplitudes for every matrix of a known support, nor a minimal number of probes for identifying a structurally constrained P. Inspected the exact-rational script and distinguished the supplied finite checks from the proof; no supplied script was executed.
